main_text.head: DISSERTATIONIS CHRONOLOGICÆ S A C R Æ Pars Prior De Demonstrationum ad figendam justam nati Christi epocham hactenus allatarum insufficientiâ.
CAPUT I.

head.i: Traditionis, annum Christi natalem definientis, insufficientia.

main_text.p: §. I.ETiamsi æra vulgaris (quæ à nato Christo usque in hunc diem annos 1698 præterlapsos computat) à quibusdam ex traditionum quadam veneratione ut satis accurata & vera suscipiatur, & ob ecclesiæ Romanæ authoritatem (quæ eam sanè suscepit) mordicus defendatur: nihilominus inter ipsos Pontificios invenias, qui eam cum rei veritate minus consentire ingenuè agnoscunt. Desideratur sanè in istâ æra (ut traditionis apostolicæ titulo gaudeat) requisita antiquitas: qui enim hanc æram

page.notes: The initial "E" is a woodcut ornamental letter, joined to "Tiamsi" as "ETiamsi". The word "hactenus" in the title is set with a ligature and reads as "hactenus"; the form is clear enough but the ligature makes it slightly uncertain. The printed hyphens at line ends ("traditio-num", "authorita-tem", "Desi-deratur", "insuffi-cientia") are joined in the transcription.
